# `export type` for [core](/commands/categories/core.md)

<div class='command-title'>Give a name to a type annotation and export it from a module.</div>

## Command Type

`keyword`

## Signature

```> export type {flags} (name) (type)```

## Parameters

 -  `name`: Name of the type alias.
 -  `type`: Equals sign followed by a type, as written after `:` on a parameter.


## Input/output types:

| input   | output  |
| ------- | ------- |
| nothing | nothing |
## Examples

Export a type alias from a module and import it with a command.
```nu
> module geo {
        export type Point = record<x: int, y: int>
        export def origin []: nothing -> Point { {x: 0, y: 0} }
    }
    use geo [Point origin]
    let p: Point = origin
    $p.y
0
```

## Notes
This command is a parser keyword. `use <module> <name>`, `use <module> [<names>]` and `use <module> *` import a type alias. A bare `use <module>` doesn't, because a type alias name can't take the module name as a prefix the way a command name does.

For details, check:
  https://www.nushell.sh/book/thinking_in_nu.html
